description: The bar chart illustrates the “effect” scores—likely representing model performance or probing accuracy—of six different multilingual BERT variants (mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, XLM-B₂) across nine language families or categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to 30 with major tick marks at intervals of 10, and each bar is accompanied by error bars indicating variability or confidence intervals. The horizontal axis groups the language families, with “IE-Slavic” labeled as “IE-Slavic family” for clarity. Within each group, the six models are represented by distinct colors as indicated in the legend: mBERT-L₂ (light gray), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). The bars are not sorted by height within groups, and no single model consistently outperforms others across all families. Notably, IE-Indic shows the highest effect scores overall, particularly for mBERT-R₂ and XLM-B₂, both exceeding 20. In contrast, Isolate and Uralic show very low effect scores across all models, mostly below 5. Semitic exhibits moderate performance, with XLM-L₂ and mBERT-B₂ reaching around 15–16. The chart visually suggests that model performance varies significantly by language family, with Indo-European branches generally yielding higher scores than isolates or Uralic languages.
